intro.text: An ancient, legendary city, said to have been the home of the Knights Radiant and the centre of the Silver Kingdoms during the Heraldic Epochs.
The ancient tower-city of the Knights Radiant, high in the mountains of Ur at the centre of Roshar, rediscovered by the Alethi as the Everstorm came.
The Radiants' tower-city, sealed behind a dome of light after the contest, with its Oathgates inactive but its Towerlight-powered systems still working.

description.text: Urithiru stands almost exactly at the centre of the continent, in the western part of the mountains of Ur on the border of Emul and Greater Hexi, on the east side of a mountain, leaning against two slopes.

The tower is as wide as a city and as tall as a small mountain: ten semicircular levels of eighteen storeys each, about 2,700 feet in all, each level wider than the one above, with fields and gardens on the wider roofs. Huge plateau-sized sections jut from the bottom level, and a vast plaza lies in front.
The Breakaway, a cavern as large as a small town, became the Alethi's central market, with stalls, taverns and growing numbers of permanent buildings around a round well that never runs dry.

Its stormward side is flat, with windows facing the Origin that survived thousands of years intact. Inside, tunnels twist in strange curves, and the smooth, unscratchable stone shows bands of coloured strata like those of Kholinar's windblades.

items.text: The Stone sought a legacy in a child of Honor and Cultivation, and Urithiru was constructed about six thousand years before the Night of Sorrows.

Urithiru was the headquarters of the Knights Radiant and the centre of the Silver Kingdoms, with ten thrones, one for each king. Besides Radiants it was home to many ordinary people: servants, traders and craftsmen. At one point the Unmade Re-Shephir invaded the tower and was sealed away by a Lightweaver.
The Radiants charged for the use of the Oathgates, and shortly before the Recreance their tariffs rose to levels some thought unreasonable.
As the tower failed, Melishi withdrew from the Sibling. The Sibling linked that withdrawal to his experiments in imprisoning spren.
By the present day, Urithiru was almost unknown to Vorins who did not study the Knights Radiant; Shallan had never even heard its name.

The Shin know the tower's traditions and consider its stones fine to walk on. After becoming Truthless, Szeth often went there, passing a village at the foot of the mountain so often that the villagers began leaving him spheres as if he were a god.

Jasnah Kholin searched for the city, convinced a Desolation was coming. Shallan finished her work and found ancient Stormseat at the centre of the Shattered Plains, now the Parshendi city of Narak, and as the Everstorm was summoned she used its Oathgate to bring the Alethi army to Urithiru.
With the parshmen gone, the Alethi pressed low-nahn darkeyes, soldiers and caravan workers into hauling water, and Adolin encouraged them to form a water haulers' guild to bargain for wages.
The tower is above the storms, so Stormlight was scarce at first and infused spheres were worth more than face value; once the highstorms returned, spheres were lowered into them in large cages.
Dalinar named Sebarial Highprince of Commerce, and Sebarial planned to tax passage through the Oathgates to fund the city.

Shallan cut her way into a hidden chamber below the ground floor, where she confronted Re-Shephir, who fled through a long tunnel of caverns to the foothills of the Tu Fallia mountains. Navani's scholars later made the chamber a meeting hall for those studying the tower.

Without its old mechanisms, the city struggled: crops would not grow, so it depended on trade and salvage from the warcamps; plumbing clogged, privies had long lines, Soulcasters worked constantly to clear waste, and heating was a constant problem.
Before the battle at Thaylen City, the enemy attacked Urithiru through the Kholinar Oathgate, and after some early success they were driven back out.

In the year that followed, Navani planned the Ten Rings, an orderly part of the Breakaway with lower taxes and regular patrols, and the Cloudwalk, a garden balcony on the eighth tier, became a favourite place for people of every nation and rank.
About a year into the True Desolation, a large force of Fused attacked the tower and began corrupting the Sibling at its central pillar, leaving every Radiant there but Kaladin unconscious.
During the occupation, the Sibling revealed their powers to Kaladin, Dabbid and Navani, and bonded Navani, making her a Bondsmith and bringing the tower fully back to life.
Working fabrials restored plumbing, ventilation and temperature control. Lights and warmth supported crops intended to make the city self-sufficient.
In Shadesmar, the awakened tower appeared as a glowing crystalline structure known as Nohadon's Stairways.
A dome of solid light enclosed Urithiru, cutting it off from the rest of Roshar. The Oathgates stopped working, but Towerlight and the city's fabrials remained available.
With Navani unconscious and the Sibling unresponsive, Renarin and Jasnah began working toward representative government instead of a monarchy.
